newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan tightens credit limits as stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan tightens credit limits as stocks rise.

text.p: The Taiwan stock market's rise above 9,600 points on Friday has activated an anti-speculation mechanism under which regulators will tighten credit trading limits starting on Saturday, authorities said.
Taiwan's watchdog Securities and Futures Commission said in a statement that margin-buying and short-selling ratios would be trimmed by 10 percentage points each to 30 and 40 percent, respectively.

To avoid excessive credit expansion at the time of sharp stock market rallies, Taiwan sets benchmarks to reduce credit trading limits when the index passes 6,000, 7,200, 8,400 point and 9,600 points, the commission said.
The index surpassed 8,400 points on March 17.
The benchmark stock index closed 105.6 points or 1.1 percent higher at 9,677.4 on Friday -- the market's highest level since April 27, 1990.
Turnover was very heavy at T$218 billion.

According to rules, the margin-buying ratio or margin loan ratio -- the degree to which securities finance firms can lend to investors for buying shares -- would fall to 30 percent of a share's purchase price from 40 percent.

The short-selling or stock-loan ratio -- margin requirements for shares investors can borrow from securities finance firms for short selling -- would be reduced to 40 percent of a share's selling price from 50 percent.
The exchange has said the rules aim to limit financial risks and prevent the stock market from overheating.
